column2: Outwitting the opponents Still building upon the concepts developed in year 7 and 8, teaching will focus more so on demonstrating control, consistency and fluency aspects of outwitting the opponents. This will be taught through scenarios in gameplay and isolated situations.
column3: Identifying and solving Problems Still building upon the concepts developed in year 7 and 8, teaching will focus more the application of problems solving skills to specific scenarios (differentiated) set by the teacher. These should encompass and encourage the students to show a wide variety of problem solving skills.
column4: Accurate Replication Still building upon the concepts developed in year 7 and 8, teaching will focus more the application core and advanced skills to specific scenarios (differentiated) set by the teacher. These should encompass and encourage the students to show a wide variety of core and advanced skills and provide the platform for students analysing performance and refining technique
column5: Exploring and Communicating Ideas Still building upon the concepts developed in year 7 and 8, teaching will centre around giving students the freedom of exploration through the effective use of scenarios. Again this is something that could be built into previous years. For example in gymnastics the teacher might assign each group with 3 roles, an aesthetic coach, a technical coach and a transition of moves coach
column6: Exercising safely and effectively   If commencing the exercising safely and effectively unit students should now have an understanding of responses and adaptations to the different systems of the body to exercise.
column7: Performing at Maximum Levels  Teaching will centre around giving the opportunity to demonstrate their best performances in a variety of different scenarios. For example in tennis a student might wish to develop his serving technique as he / she only currently achieves 10% of first serves. The conditioned game could focus on a points scoring system where points are awarded for successful first serves. Students are also assessed in their GCSE terminology themes they have covered throughout teh year. The test is a multiple choice test and students get a GCSE equivalent grade
